title: Fourier characters have unit modulus
statement: Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ be the primitive $k$-th root of unity. For $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, let $\chi_s \colon \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \bbc$ be the Fourier character $\chi_s(x) = \omega_k^{\,s\cdot x}$, where $s \cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ is the componentwise dot product. Then for every $s, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$ one has $\abs{\chi_s(x)} = 1$.
hypotheses_covered: k is nonzero (k ≥ 1), giving a well-defined ω_k
